root_cause.text: AF_RXRPC’s ACK parsing code assumed the received sk_buff could be safely made linear with `skb_condense()` and then directly read the SACK table from `skb->data`, but `skb_condense()` can fail to flatten fragmented UDP packets, leading to incorrect/out-of-bounds access and parsing of the ACK SACK table in `rxrpc_input_soft_acks()`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch replaces `u8 *acks = skb->data + ...` with copying the SACK table out via `skb_copy_bits()` into a local `sack[256]` buffer, explicitly notes that “skb_condense() can silently fail to do anything,” and removes `skb_condense(skb)` from `rxrpc_input_ack()`, showing the bug was reliance on a possibly non-linear skb being treated as flat memory.

vuln_statements.content: u8 *acks = skb->data + sizeof(struct rxrpc_wire_header) + sizeof(struct rxrpc_ackpacket);

intent_record.intent_summary: Copy the SACK table into a local aligned buffer before parsing it to correctly handle extended SACKs and avoid unsafe direct skb access.
intent_record.what: The code now allocates a local 256-byte, unsigned-long-aligned buffer named `sack`, copies the SACK data from the skb into that buffer with `skb_copy_bits()`, zero-initializes it first, and sets `acks` to point at this local buffer. It also introduces `nsack` to hold the copied length limited to 256. Inside the loop, it resets `acks` to `sack` whenever `i & 255` is zero, and removes the old logic that tried to rewind the `acks` pointer and reset `i` when `i == 256`.
intent_record.how: This changes SACK processing so the function no longer reads directly from skb memory while iterating over ACK/NACK bits. Instead, it works from a bounded local copy of the SACK table, which supports both normal and extended SACK formats and avoids pointer arithmetic over the packet buffer. This makes parsing safer and correctly handles larger SACK tables without relying on the original skb layout during iteration.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove unnecessary skb condensation from RXRPC ACK input handling.
intent_record.what: The code removes the conditional call to `skb_condense(skb)` inside `rxrpc_input_ack()`, deleting the `if (nr_acks > 0)` block entirely while leaving the surrounding ACK parsing and timestamp/sequence assignments unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, ACK handling no longer repacks the socket buffer after processing one or more ACKs. This avoids the extra buffer compaction work and any side effects associated with modifying the skb contents during ACK input processing, while preserving the rest of the ACK state update logic.
